Every major objective was met, providing critical data to inform designs of the next generation Starship and Super Heavy. stories.title: [YT] Starship - Test Like You Fly
stories.excerpt: Three years since the first flight of Starship, the next generation is here. New ship. New booster. New engines. New pad and new test site. SpaceX engineers are working to solve one of the most difficult engineering challenges in history: developing a fully, rapidly reusable rocket. “Test Like You Fly” launches a series that takes you inside the factories and onto the launch pads where humanity's future in space is unfolding. featured.title: Vulcan failure investigation focuses on ‘inadequate fuel supply’ to booster engines
featured.excerpt: United Launch Alliance said Wednesday that a preliminary review of flight data points to an inadequate supply of fuel to the Blue Origin-manufactured engines of its Vulcan rocket, rather than a problem with the engines themselves, as the reason Sunday's launch fell short of orbit with 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites aboard.
featured.summary: Spaceflight Now reports that a preliminary ULA review of Vulcan's flight data points to inadequate fuel supply to its Blue Origin-built booster engines rather than an engine fault as the likely cause of the launch's failure to reach orbit with its 40 Amazon Leo satellites.
